messages:
maya: folks, hitting pod networking errors when scaling the new GPU nodepool in ap-southeast-3. Pods stuck in ContainerCreating with ENI/IPv4 allocation failures. Need quota asks and short mitigations so rollout doesn't block other work.

infra-bot: Please include account id, VPC id, region, instance types, current quotas, and any logs. Use quota template: https://intranet.redwood/infra/quota-template

aj: Account 987654321012, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, region ap-southeast-3. Trying to scale a g5.12x nodepool to 12 nodes. Node pod density ~22 GPU pods/node. Errors in kubelet: "failed to create pod sandbox: networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod" and EC2 errors: "InvalidParameterValue: No available IPs in subnet".

devon: Quick triage: looks like two bottlenecks. 1) Subnet/secondary IP headroom is almost exhausted (our node subnets are /24s carved from a /22). 2) We have a conservative EC2 quota for g5 family in this region (soft limit ~20). What I recommend we request: 
- Increase instance quota for g5 family (On-Demand + Spot) to 60 in ap-southeast-3
- Increase Elastic Network Interfaces quota (per-region) to 250
- Expand VPC addressing: add a /21 secondary CIDR or expand node subnets to provide ~2000 usable addresses

aj: Short-term mitigation while support approves: rollback nodepool to 6 nodes, set kubelet max-pods to 16 on GPU nodes, and tune aws-cni WARM_IP_TARGET to 10. That should reduce immediate IP consumption.

maya: kubectl describe output: 

```
Warning FailedAttachVolume  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "eni-xxxxx": request returned error: InvalidParameterValue: No available IPs in subnet
FailedCreatePodSandBox kubelet, networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod
```

maya: Also attaching a prometheus snapshot link to show IP usage trend for the last 24h.

devon: did a quick calc for the ticket: target steady-state 30 GPU nodes * avg 3 ENIs/node * 12 secondary IPs per ENI ~= 1080 IPs. Our /22 gives ~1024 total addresses, of which ~600 usable for pods after infra reservations. So /21 (2048) makes sense.

sre-liaison: I've opened ticket INC-2026-799 with the cloud provider: requested g5 quota -> 60, ENI quota -> 250, and allocation of a /21 secondary CIDR to VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d in ap-southeast-3. Provider asked for steady-state numbers and a test/scale plan. They also asked if we need EIP quota bumps (we do not).

aj: For the justification section: steady-state required 30 GPU nodes, avg pods per node 18, burst for training jobs up to 45 nodes. We plan to move to committed/reserved capacity later; this is a short-term on-demand need. Include cost estimate: ~30 * g5.12x hourly = ~cost TBD in ticket.

devon: Ops steps to run now: 
1) set AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_WARM_IP_TARGET=10 in aws-node daemonset env and rollout restart.
2) apply node annotation to gpu nodegroup to set kubelet max-pods=16.
3) rollback new nodepool to previous size and cordon/migrate noncritical pods.

maya: Provider replied preliminary approval for ENI bump to 150 pending CIDR expansion. They asked for the exact secondary CIDR size (/21) and confirmation of the VPC id and whether we have any routing overlap. Sent them our requested /21 and prometheus snapshots. They also asked for expected pace of scaling; I provided our autoscaler policy (max surge 10 nodes per 10m).

aj: handy commands for diagnostic and counts: 
```
# list current secondary IP usage across nodes
kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=nodepool=gpu | awk '{print $6}' | tail -n +2 | wc -l

# check aws ENI quotas
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A --region ap-southeast-3
```

devon: I'll add links to the autoscaler policy and the rollout playbook in the ticket. Once CIDR added we request final ENI and instance quota increases.

maya: Thanks everyone. Will coordinate canary rollback at 02:00 UTC and update the ticket. Marking thread resolved for now and will reopen if provider requests more info. :thumbsup:
